subject: spanish
source_note: Topic structure follows the Pearson Edexcel A-Level Spanish specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Changes in society
units.blurb: La evolución de la sociedad española — family, work and tourism in Spain

units.name: Political and artistic culture
units.blurb: Music, media, festivals and traditions across the Spanish-speaking world

units.name: Immigration & aspects of political life
units.blurb: Immigration and multicultural Spain, plus Franco's dictatorship and the transition

units.name: Literary texts and film
units.blurb: Critical study of two prescribed Spanish works

units.name: Independent research project
units.blurb: Researching, presenting and discussing a chosen subject

topics.name: Changing Family Structures
topics.blurb: El cambio en la estructura familiar: evolving attitudes to marriage, relationships and families

topics.name: The World of Work
topics.blurb: El mundo laboral: working life, job opportunities for young people and gender equality

topics.name: The Impact of Tourism
topics.blurb: El impacto turístico: economic, social and environmental effects of tourism on Spain

topics.name: Music
topics.blurb: La música: changes, trends and the impact of music on contemporary culture

topics.name: The Media
topics.blurb: Los medios de comunicación: TV, telenovelas, print and online media and their social/political impact

topics.name: Festivals & Traditions
topics.blurb: Los festivales y las tradiciones: festivals, fiestas, customs and traditions

topics.name: Positive Impact of Immigration
topics.blurb: El impacto positivo: immigrants' contributions to Spain's economy and culture

topics.name: Challenges of Immigration & Integration
topics.blurb: Local-community measures; marginalisation and isolation from the immigrant viewpoint

topics.name: Reaction to Immigration
topics.blurb: La reacción social y pública: political approaches and public opinion on immigration

topics.name: Civil War & the Rise of Franco
topics.blurb: La Guerra Civil (1936-1939): republicans vs nationalists and divisions in society

topics.name: The Franco Dictatorship
topics.blurb: La dictadura franquista: daily life under Franco, political oppression and censorship

topics.name: Transition to Democracy
topics.blurb: La transición: King Juan Carlos, the Suárez government and the 1981 coup attempt

topics.name: Study of Two Prescribed Works
topics.blurb: Two discrete Spanish works: two texts, or one text and one film, from the prescribed list

topics.name: Critical & Analytical Response
topics.blurb: Analysing key issues, themes and characterisation; building justified arguments

topics.name: Form, Technique & Context
topics.blurb: Narrative voice, camera work, and the social and cultural setting of the works

topics.name: Choosing & Researching a Subject
topics.blurb: Selecting a subject on Spanish-speaking society/culture and gathering written sources

topics.name: Presenting & Summarising Sources
topics.blurb: Summarising at least two written sources and giving a personal response

topics.name: Discussing the Research
topics.blurb: Answering questions and sustaining a wider discussion on the research findings

connections.why: Gender equality and changing family roles are closely tied to shifts in the world of work
Tourism is a major source of jobs and economic opportunity in Spain
Festivals and traditions are central to Spain's tourist appeal and identity
Music is woven through Spain's fiestas, festivals and cultural traditions
Media platforms drive the trends and reach that shape contemporary music
Media coverage strongly shapes public opinion and political debate on immigration
The benefits immigrants bring sit alongside the challenges of integration
Marginalisation experienced by immigrants feeds and is shaped by public reaction
Immigration reshapes the demographics and structure of Spanish society and families
Franco's victory in the Civil War established the dictatorship that followed
The end of the dictatorship led directly into Spain's transition to democracy
The end of censorship transformed Spain's media landscape after Franco
Spain's authoritarian past informs modern debates about identity and openness
Studying the prescribed works is the basis for critical and analytical essays
Strong analysis weaves together themes, technique and social/cultural context
Many prescribed works are set against the Civil War and Franco era studied in Theme 4
Social themes from Theme 1 recur in the prescribed texts and films
A well-chosen subject and good sources are what students then summarise and present
The presentation of sources launches the wider discussion that follows
Source-analysis and argument skills from the works transfer to the research project
Multicultural and political themes make rich, well-resourced research subjects
